page: Amazon Web Services m6idn.metal is a bare-metal, general-purpose server powered by Intel Xeon 8375C processors. It features 128 vCPUs across 64 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, operating at a clock speed of 3.5 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 512 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, the server is equipped with 7600 GB of NVMe SSD instance store volumes. Network connectivity is highly optimized, delivering a baseline bandwidth of 200 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate top-tier multi-core performance, with the server scoring in the top 10% for stress-ng multi-core CPU tests, PassMark CPU scores, and PassMark CPU encryption and extended instructions tests. It also achieves top-tier results in Geekbench ray tracing and image processing. Memory bandwidth is strong, reaching 6743.81 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 339.12 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. Single-core performance, however, sits in the average tier, as evidenced by stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores.

The m6idn.metal instance offers high resource density and high-speed local storage, making it qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads requiring massive parallel processing and high-throughput I/O without the overhead of virtualization. However, its lack of GPU acceleration makes it poorly suited for heavy deep learning tasks; for instance, large-model LLM text generation falls into the bottom 25% of performance. This server is best suited for high-performance databases, Redis deployments, large-scale software compilation, static web serving, and multi-threaded data processing applications.
